popup.bridgeResilience.noDecay: No distance-decay metrics for this bridge ({mode}). Switch "Weighting" to "Unweighted by distance".
popup.bridgeResilience.weightNoteText: Distance decay: destination weight = population × exp(−baseline drive time / 20 min); τ = 20 min is an assumption. Impact = sum of village population × mean extra seconds. Ranks compare single bridges within the same transport mode.
popup.bridgeResilience.modeNotInGraph: This bridge is not in the {mode} road network
popup.bridgeResilience.modelNoAffected: The model found no affected origin–destination pairs
popup.bridgeResilience.fpBarrier: Higher when the water span is longer and there are fewer river-crossing roads within ±3 km up/downstream. Independent of transport mode; same value for car and motorcycle.
popup.bridgeResilience.fpNetwork: Total impact under distance decay (τ = 20 min, assumed) in person-seconds
popup.bridgeResilience.fpPopulation: Population whose average trip takes more than 30 s extra; 0 for most bridges, ties share the average rank.
popup.bridgeResilience.fpRedundancy: Share of affected O–D pairs that do not reroute via an alternative bridge within 5 km on the same river, plus the average detour ratio. Higher means poorer alternatives.
popup.bridgeResilience.fpCautionGuandu: Guandu and Danjiang are about 7 km apart, beyond the "same river 5 km" rule, so each counts 0% as the other's alternative. Half of their high lack-of-alternatives score comes from this rule.
popup.bridgeResilience.fpCautionXinbei: The water span of Xinbei Bridge is taken from the skewed motorcycle lane, so it is an upper bound.
popup.bridgeResilience.fpVariant: With no distance limit, bridges tens of kilometres upstream also count as alternatives, so the default stays at 5 km on the same river. The variant is for comparison only.
popup.bridgeResilience.fpRead: Each of the four dimensions is ranked among 73 single bridges (26 manually reviewed + 47 auto-selected). They are not summed into a total score. These are failure consequences, not risk.
popup.bridgeResilience.destIntro: Starting from this village ({mode}), which districts become slower to reach when the bridge is closed. Affected = more than 60 s extra; average and maximum count only affected destinations.
popup.bridgeResilience.destUniformNote: Destination details use the unweighted version (no distance-decay data), so they differ from the current distance-decay village colours. For a consistent basis, switch "Weighting" back to "Unweighted by distance".
popup.bridgeResilience.destError: Failed to load destination data. Please click the village again later.
popup.bridgeResilience.destIdle: No destination data for this village in this scenario.
popup.bridgeResilience.destNoSlowButUnre: No destinations are slowed down, but some are unreachable (see below).
popup.bridgeResilience.destNoAffected: No other village is affected from this village (extra time does not exceed 60 s). This is not a measured "0 minutes"; it is below the threshold.
popup.bridgeResilience.unreachable: Unreachable: {label}, {villages} village(s), {pop} (not counted in extra time)
popup.bridgeResilience.mapNote: Map colours show the mean extra time of the destination district (same colour within a district; there are no per-village values). Blue outlines mark the top {n} affected villages; the thick white outline is the origin.
popup.bridgeResilience.jointToggle: Close together with the other bridge
popup.bridgeResilience.clickVillage: Click a village on the map to see where it becomes slower to reach.
popup.bridgeResilience.noMetrics: No simulation metrics for this bridge.
popup.bridgeResilience.fpDetailSummary: How the four dimensions are calculated
popup.bridgeResilience.researchStatusTex: Work in progress; site-owner only (BSS licence on HOLD). These are single-bridge failure consequences, not risk.
popup.bridgeResilience.bridgeScopeText: 73 bridges: 26 manually reviewed + 47 auto-selected by bridge selection v7 (machine matching of road segment groups, not yet manually reviewed)
popup.bridgeResilience.p90LossBan: p90 {p90}; loss {loss} (for comparison, not the main result)
popup.bridgeResilience.altRouteText: Only the 3 representative O–D pairs with the largest registered-population weight are drawn; not necessarily the longest detours.
